gw_mip.in.all: Connections: taken on every address of the server.
gw_mip.in.only: Connections: taken only on {ips}. The ports of the protocols and 443 of the own site are closed on the other addresses; SSH, forwards and port 80 stay open everywhere. IPv6 addresses are not limited by this list: they have an intake of their own. Containers and other VPNs on this server cannot reach the protocols on the other addresses either.
gw_mip.in.all_gone: ! The chosen addresses ({ips}) are not on the server now — connections are taken on every address until they come back.
gw_mip.in.some_gone: ! The chosen address {ips} is not on the server now — nothing is taken on it.
gw_mip.in.back: Take connections on every address again: {back} (or the SSH menu 17 → 4 → “Taking connections” → 1).
gw_mip.in.set_only: Done: the protocols take connections only on {ips}. To undo: {back}.
gw_mip.in.set_all: Done: the protocols take connections on every address of the server.
gw_mip.src.gone: ! Exit “{name}”: the address {ip} is not on the server now — it connects from the main address for now.
gw_mip.h4.differ: On the “direct” route devices go online from two addresses: WireGuard, AmneziaWG, OpenVPN, IKEv2, L2TP, PPTP and SSTP — from {kernel}, VLESS and the other protocols through xray — from {xray} (the address of the system’s route). It was so before the update too; Kaskad does not change it by itself.
gw_mip.src.bench: The server check measures the channel of the main address.
gw_mip.src.tg: The “Telegram API proxy” always connects to the VLESS, Hysteria2, Shadowsocks, Trojan and VMess exits from the main address (to the AmneziaWG exits too while the gateway is off): the chosen address works for the gateway.
gw_mip.src.unset: Done: exits — {n}, connect by the system’s route (the main address).
gw_mip.err.in_empty: Give at least one address. To take connections on every address: {back}.
gw_mip.err.not_here: The address {ip} is not on the server now — nothing can be taken on it. There are: {known}. To take connections on every address: {back}.
gw_mip.err.client_out: Clients connect to {ip} (the client address), and it is not in the list — the devices would lose the connection. Change the client address first (SSH menu 17 → 4) or add {ip} to the list. To undo: {back}.
gw_mip.err.host_not_in: The protocols take connections only on {ips} (“Taking connections”), and {ip} is not in that list — devices would not connect to this address. First add {ip} to it: kaskadctl gw addresses in {add} (or the SSH menu 17 → 4 → “Taking connections”), or take connections on every address again: {back}.
gw_mip.err.panel_out: The panel and the subscription links are open on {ip}, and it is not in the list: the subscriptions on the devices would stop updating and the panel would stop opening. Better give the panel a domain (its A records can be changed later) or switch the open mode of the panel on again on the chosen address. To undo: {back}.
gw_mip.err.via_out: You opened the panel through {ip}, and it is not in the list — the panel would close for you. Open the panel through a chosen address or set the list in the SSH menu. To undo: {back}.
gw_mip.err.exit_or_group: Give an exit or --group, one of the two.
gw_mip.err.no_exits: There are no exits in what was chosen.
gw_mip.err.not_exit: {id} is not an exit of the list of exits (or its key is not parsed).
gw_mip.err.route_other: An answer from {ip} does not leave through the gateway of the main address (source routing) — such an address does not suit an AmneziaWG exit: the hoster would drop the packets. A VLESS, Hysteria2, Shadowsocks, Trojan or VMess exit — it does.
gw_mip.err.same_endpoint: Another AmneziaWG exit goes to the same server {ep} with another address — two legs to one server can only share one address. Give the address to both exits (--group) or to none.
gw_mip.err.not_here6: The IPv6 {ip} is not on the server now — nothing can be taken on it. There are: {known}. To take connections on every address: {back}.
gw_mip.err.via6_out: You opened the panel over IPv6 {ip}, and the panel domain ({domain}) has no A record on an IPv4 address that takes connections: after saving the panel won’t open for you. Keep accepting on {ip} or add an A record. To undo: {back}.
gw_mip.err.in6_how: Give the IPv6 addresses, or --all (every IPv6 takes connections), or --none (none does). To take connections on every address: {back}.
gw_mip.err.not_public6: {value} isn’t an external IPv6 address. A global address of this server is needed, for example 2001:db8:10::5.
gw_mip.err.src_family: The exit “{name}” connects over IPv6 ({host}), and the IPv4 address {ip} is chosen: the exit won’t connect so. An exit over IPv6 goes from the address of the IPv6 route — keep “by the route” (main).
gw_mip.warn.domain_out: Domain {domain}: the A records {ips} are not among the chosen addresses; whoever connects by them loses the connection. Fix the A records at the registrar.
gw_mip.warn.domain_unknown: Domain {domain}: Kaskad does not know where its A records point — check them at the registrar: all must be among the chosen addresses.
gw_mip.warn.ssh_out: You are connected by SSH through {ip}, and it is not in the list: SSH stays open, but the protocols on {ip} close.
gw_mip.warn.limits: Answer only from the main address {primary}: {what} — on the other addresses devices behind NAT (phones, routers) won’t connect to them.
gw_mip.warn.gw_off: The gateway is off: while it is off the protocols and the site take connections on every address; the panel in the open mode — only on the chosen ones already.
gw_mip.warn.src_gw_off: The gateway is off: the AmneziaWG exits connect from the main address while it is off (the “Telegram API proxy” too).
gw_mip.warn.ssh6_out: You are connected by SSH through the IPv6 {ip}, and it is not in the list: SSH stays open, but the protocols on {ip} close.
gw_mip.warn.gw_off6: The gateway is off: the IPv6 intake is saved and starts working when the gateway is turned on.
gw_mip.log.src: Server addresses: the exits {exits} connect from {ip}
gw_mip.log.in_all_gone: Server addresses: the chosen addresses ({ips}) are gone — connections are taken on every address
gw_mip.log.in_gone: Server addresses: the address {ips} is not on the server — nothing is taken on it
gw_mip.log.in_back: Server addresses: the address {ips} is back on the server
gw_mip.log.src_gone: Server addresses: exit “{name}” connects from the main address for now — {ip} is gone
gw_mip.log.src_back: Server addresses: exit “{name}” connects from {ip} again
gw_mip.lock.domain_out: the panel domain {domain} has an A record on {ips}: the panel and the site stop opening on that address, and a browser may land right there
gw_mip.lock.domain_unknown: Kaskad doesn’t know the A records of the panel domain {domain}: if one of them leads to a closed address ({ips}), the panel won’t open there
gw_mip.lock.aaaa: {domain} has an AAAA record on {ip}: devices with IPv6 will go there and fail to connect — delete the AAAA record or keep accepting
gw_mip.lock.panel6: you opened the panel over IPv6 {ip}; after saving the browser moves to IPv4 ({domain} → {ip4})
gw_mip.lock.aaaa_unknown: Kaskad doesn’t know the AAAA records of the panel domain {domain}: if one of them leads to a closed IPv6 ({ips}), the panel won’t open there over IPv6
gw_mip.confirm.cli: Confirm in the panel or repeat with --yes: {cmd}
gw_mip.in6.only: IPv6 intake: only on {ips}; the ports of the protocols are closed on the other IPv6 (SSH, forwards, port 80 and ICMPv6 stay open).
gw_mip.in6.none: IPv6 intake: on no address — the ports of the protocols are closed over IPv6 (SSH, forwards, port 80 and ICMPv6 stay open); IPv4 takes connections as chosen.
gw_mip.in6.all_gone: The chosen IPv6 ({ips}) are not on the server now: no connections over IPv6 until the address is back or another one is chosen.
gw_mip.in6.set_all: Done: the protocols take connections on every IPv6 address.
gw_mip.in6.set_only: Done: over IPv6 the protocols take connections only on {ips}. To undo: {back}.
gw_mip.in6.set_none: Done: over IPv6 the protocols take connections on no address. To undo: {back}.
gw_mip.ip6.pre6: The chain gw_pre6 (IPv6 intake) is not as chosen: there is {got}, {want} is needed
gw_mip.err.give4_later: Giving out IPv4 addresses comes in the next release. For now only an IPv6 of this server can go into the subscription as an extra line.
gw_mip.err.give6_not_here: IPv6 {ip} isn’t on the server now — it can’t be given out. There are: {known}.
gw_mip.err.give6_deprecated: IPv6 {ip} is deprecated: the hoster will take it away soon — it can’t be given out. Choose a current address.
gw_mip.err.give6_no_route: IPv6 {ip} has no way out (no default IPv6 route, or the answer leaves another way): devices won’t connect over it.
gw_mip.err.give6_echo_other: From outside {ip} is seen as {seen} (the hoster’s NAT or proxy): devices won’t connect over {ip}.
gw_mip.err.give6_body: Send ip6: an IPv6 address of this server, or null to take the IPv6 lines out of the subscription.
gw_mip.warn.give6_unchecked: {ip} couldn’t be checked from outside (the IPv6 echo didn’t answer): the lines are given out, but the address isn’t checked from outside.
gw_mip.warn.give6_dynamic: {ip} was assigned automatically (SLAAC) and may change: then the IPv6 lines leave the subscription until you choose the new address.
gw_mip.warn.give6_limits: {what} answer only from the address of the IPv6 route ({src}) — they get no IPv6 line on this address.
gw_mip.warn.give6_in6: IPv6 {ip} now takes connections: “Accept and hand out” includes accepting them.
gw_mip.warn.in6_closes_give: IPv6 {ip} is given out as a subscription line: while it takes no connections the subscription has no IPv6 lines. To stop giving it: {back}.
gw_mip.lock.give6_listen_on: VLESS Reality starts listening on IPv6 too: xray restarts — the open VLESS and Hysteria2 connections reconnect
gw_mip.lock.give6_listen_off: VLESS Reality stops listening on IPv6: xray restarts, and devices that picked the VLESS “· IPv6” line by hand stay offline until the subscription refreshes
gw_mip.log.give6: Server addresses: the extra IPv6 subscription line — {ip}
gw_mip.give6.set: Done: {ip} goes into the subscription as an extra line after the IPv4 ones — for VLESS Reality, Hysteria2, WireGuard and AmneziaWG (Hysteria2 with the mask and AmneziaWG on the userspace AmneziaWG engine — only when it is the IPv6 route address); files and QR codes stay on IPv4. To undo: {back}.
gw_mip.give6.unset: Done: the subscription has no IPv6 lines any more (the apps drop them at the next refresh).
gw_mip.give6.idle: ! IPv6 {ip} is chosen for the subscription but isn’t given out now: {why}. To drop the choice: {back}.
gw_mip.give6.why.echo_other: it’s seen from outside as another address
gw_mip.err.role_family: {ip} is IPv6, and “direct” and “for exits” take IPv4 only: devices and exits go online over IPv4.
gw_mip.err.role_not_here: The address {ip} isn’t on the server now — it can’t be chosen. There are: {known}. To reset the choice: {back}.
gw_mip.err.not_out: {ip} isn’t “for exits”: turn “For exits” on for it first. To reset the choice: {back}.
gw_mip.err.direct_route: An answer from {ip} doesn’t leave through the gateway of the route address (source routing): “direct” traffic from it would take the wrong way. To reset the choice: {back}.
gw_mip.err.direct_needed: The route address {route} isn’t “for exits”, so “direct” must go from another address. Turn “For exits” on for {route} or choose another address. To reset the choice: {back}.
gw_mip.err.out_last: {ip} is the last address “for exits”: at least one must stay. To reset the choice: {back}.
gw_mip.err.out_no_other: “Direct” or exits go from {ip}, and there is no other address “for exits” with a working route — nowhere to move them. To reset the choice: {back}.
gw_mip.err.direct_body: Send ip: an IPv4 address of this server, or null for “direct” from the route address.
gw_mip.err.out_body: Send ip (an IPv4 address of this server) and on: true or false.
gw_mip.warn.direct_gw_off: The gateway is off: the choice of “direct” is saved and starts working when the gateway is turned on.
gw_mip.lock.out_own: the server’s own traffic (updates, the bot) stays on the route address {route}
gw_mip.direct.set: Done: “direct” traffic of every protocol goes from {ip} — sites see it. The server’s own traffic (updates, the bot) goes from the route address {route}.
gw_mip.direct.unset: Done: “direct” goes from the route address again.
gw_mip.direct.line: “Direct”: sites see {ip} (every protocol); the server’s own traffic goes from the route address {route}.
gw_mip.direct.idle: “Direct” from {ip} isn’t working now ({why}) — sites see the route address {route}.
gw_mip.direct.why.gone: the address isn’t on the server
gw_mip.direct.why.route: an answer from it leaves past the gateway of the route address
gw_mip.out.moved: “Direct” and the exits that went from it now go from {to}.
gw_mip.reset.done: Done: the choice of “for exits”, “direct” and IPv6 in the subscription is reset — everything is as by default. Taking connections and the addresses of the exits are unchanged.
gw_mip.log.reset: Server addresses: the choice of “for exits”, “direct” and IPv6 in the subscription is reset
gw_mip.log.direct_gone: Server addresses: “direct” from {ip} isn’t working for now — sites see the route address
gw_mip.err.src_route_out: The route address {ip} isn’t “for exits”: “by the system’s route” the exit would connect from it. Choose an address “for exits” for the exit or turn “For exits” on for {ip}. To reset the choice: {back}.
gw_mip.out.route_loose: The route address {ip} isn’t “for exits”, yet the exits {names} without an address of their own connect from it. Choose an address “for exits” for them: kaskadctl gw addresses exit ID IP.
gw_mip.out.moved_exits: The exits that went from it now go from {to}.
